ai.title: Remove escape key clear input action
ai.summary: The CLI now only clears the input buffer when Ctrl+C is pressed, removing the Escape key from this action. This change prevents accidental input loss, specifically addressing concerns from vim users who rely on Escape for other navigation tasks. The modification is localized to `cli/src/utils/keyboard-actions.ts` in the `resolveChatKeyboardAction` function. The `clear-input` action type remains available but is now exclusively triggered by Ctrl+C when text is present.

eli5.text: You know how pressing the Escape key on your keyboard used to clear whatever you'd typed into the chat input? That's no longer the case. Now, only pressing Ctrl+C will clear your typed message. This means if you're someone who uses Escape for other things while typing (like switching modes in vim), you won't lose what you were working on. The change went live today and only affects the part of the program that handles what happens when you press keys while typing messages.

ai.title: Lazy-init analytics in trackEvent
ai.summary: Removed explicit initAnalytics and web instrumentation.ts. Analytics client now initializes lazily inside trackEvent if missing. Uses global env for config. Prevents skipped events due to uninitialized client.

eli5.text: Events your app sends to analytics will no longer be lost just because tracking happened before the analytics client finished setting up. Instead of requiring the analytics client to be turned on ahead of time during website startup, it now quietly starts itself up the first time an event is actually recorded. If you were watching the website's startup logs, you would no longer see the usual messages about connecting analytics at the moment the site launches, because that step has been removed entirely. This is live today for the web app.

ai.title: CLI version bumped to 1.0.566
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI release package version was incremented from 1.0.565 to 1.0.566 in cli/release/package.json. This release-bump commit aggregates user-facing features and fixes shipped since the previous version, including the Gravity ads integration with new /ads:enable and /ads:disable commands, the Escape key clear-input action removal for vim users, and lazy analytics initialization in trackEvent. Additional changes include the write_todos tool returning a static message and structured logging in analytics initialization and chat completions requests.
ai.evidence: Commit 61cbc382 modifies cli/release/package.json, incrementing the version field from 1.0.565 to 1.0.566. The diff shows only this single-line version bump in the package manifest.

eli5.text: This release introduces contextual advertisements inside the CLI, adds new slash commands to enable or disable ad visibility, and displays rotating sponsored ads above the input area where ad impressions add credit back to your balance. It also refines how your todos are shown in tool results to prevent duplicated lines, switches the analytics and chat logging to a cleaner structured format so configuration details are captured consistently, and removes the Escape key action that was clearing your input so vim-style navigation no longer wipes out what you typed. Additionally, a new revenue reporting script aggregates Stripe transaction data for September through December 2025, and the billing test fixtures now include an ad-balance field so the balance preview correctly accounts for ad credits. Upgrading gives you a cleaner command line, no accidental loss of typed input when using Escape, visible ad credits earning back compute balance, and more reliable logging of analytics and chat activity without exposing sensitive keys.

ai.title: Remove initAnalytics from agent runtime tests
ai.summary: Removed `initAnalytics` mocks and calls from agent runtime tests, switching to `configureAnalytics` in analytics server tests. This aligns test suites with the new analytics initialization API. Covers `packages/agent-runtime` and `common/src`.

eli5.text: If you use the analytics testing setup for the agent runtime, the way test cases configure analytics changed: tests no longer call the old analytics setup method and instead use the newer configuration method that takes a simpler config object. If you maintain or run these tests, you'll see fewer mock setup lines in the test files (about 37 lines were removed and 6 added across the test suites). This is already live today as part of the latest code; it only affects the test/build setup, not the product behavior you see.

ai.title: Ads API drops message schema enforcement
ai.summary: `messageSchema` in `web/src/app/api/v1/ads/_post.ts` replaced with empty `z.object({})`, removing `role` and `content` validation. Ads endpoint now accepts arbitrary message objects without schema rejection. Internal API surface only.

eli5.text: The internal tool that handles ad-related data used to require every message in a request to follow a strict format (a specific role and content). Now it accepts any message structure without checking the format. Only internal systems that feed into the ads endpoint are affected, so external users won't notice anything different unless they interact directly with that internal API.

ai.title: Analytics gating switched to NEXTPUBLICCBENVIRONMENT
ai.summary: Event tracking in common/src/analytics.ts now checks env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT !== 'prod' instead of isProdEnv(analyticsConfig?.envName). This replaces the previous environment validation logic with a direct Next.js public environment variable check. Scope is limited to the shared analytics module.

eli5.text: The app now uses a simpler, single switch to decide whether to record your usage activity, and that switch has been flipped to the off position for all non-production environments. When you use the app today, the system quietly checks that one setting instead of running the older, more complex environment check before deciding whether to save your actions. Events are still tracked normally in the live production environment, so from your perspective nothing about the recording of your activity in the real app has changed.

ai.title: Simplify analytics and delete tests
ai.summary: Removed analytics config extraction and environment checks from `common/src/analytics-core.ts`, and stripped dependency injection, state management, and configuration logic from `common/src/analytics.ts`. The `trackEvent` function now initializes the PostHog client directly using environment variables, eliminating the previous indirection layers. This change affects the shared core analytics modules, simplifying the initialization flow and removing test-specific hooks.

eli5.text: The app removed several behind-the-scenes steps it used to perform to decide whether to send your usage data to the analytics system, and now instead just turns on directly when needed using settings read from the environment. You won't notice anything different while using the app today; this is internal cleanup that makes the analytics setup simpler and removes some code that only existed for testing. The change is live as of the snapshot date and doesn't add new features or change how your data is collected.

ai.title: CLI ad request sends only user and assistant messages
ai.summary: CLI `use-gravity-ad.ts` filters message history to `user` and `assistant` roles before sending to the ads API via new `convertToAdMessages` helper. Web `api/v1/ads/_post.ts` updates `messageSchema` to require `role` and `content` string fields, replacing the previous empty object schema. Gravity API 204 no-ad response moved after error check to prevent misclassification. Invalid request body errors now logged server-side.

eli5.text: When you chat with the assistant on the command line, it now only shares the messages you and the assistant typed back and forth with the ads system that finds you relevant sponsorships, instead of sending along extra internal notes. On the web side, that same ads system now checks that every message it receives has the proper role and text content, logs server-side whenever someone sends a malformed request, and waits to confirm there is no ad available before falling back to the graceful no-ad response. If you looked closely, you would notice fewer internal log entries about fetching ads and stricter validation whenever an ad request comes in.

ai.title: Fix double logging in web logger
ai.summary: Replaced `pinoLogger[level]` with direct `console[level]` calls in `logWithSync` to prevent double logging. The previous implementation caused duplicate entries because `pinoLogger` was configured to write to the same file as the sync logger. This change ensures logs are written to the file once and output to the console separately for interactive debugging.

eli5.text: When you ran the app in development, certain log messages would appear twice on your screen and get saved to the log file in duplicate. The team fixed this by telling the logging system to send each message to the screen once and to the file once, instead of accidentally sending some messages through two paths that both wrote to the same place. If you watched the terminal while developing, you will no longer see the same line printed twice for the same event.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.567 ships analytics, ads, and logging fixes
ai.summary: Freebuff CLI 1.0.567 aggregates several user-facing fixes beyond the package.json version bump in cli/release/package.json. The analytics initialization flow was simplified in common/src/analytics.ts and common/src/analytics-core.ts, replacing config extraction and DI with direct PostHog instantiation driven by NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT gating. The ads endpoint in web/src/app/api/v1/ads/_post.ts switched messageSchema to an empty z.object({}) then back to required role/content strings, while the CLI use-gravity-ad.ts helper now filters message history to user and assistant roles via convertToAdMessages. Additionally, logWithSync in the web logger was corrected to use console[level] calls instead of pinoLogger[level] to prevent duplicate log entries.
ai.evidence: Commit cbce4c13 bumps cli/release/package.json version from 1.0.566 to 1.0.567; the accompanying release updates list six prior commits (analytics init simplification, ads schema enforcement removal, ad message filtering, double logging fix, analytics env gating) as the user-visible changes in this release.

eli5.text: This release tightens up how Freebuff tracks usage and shows ads, and cleans up a logging bug that was writing duplicate entries. Analytics setup is now simpler and more reliable, switching to a direct environment check so tracking works correctly whether you're in development or production. The built-in ad system no longer enforces strict message formatting, accepting whatever conversation content is needed while filtering to only user and assistant messages for ad placement. Server-side error handling improves, with invalid ad requests now logged for debugging instead of failing silently. Upgrading gives you cleaner, non-duplicated activity logs, more stable ad delivery, and a smoother experience with fewer background errors.

ai.title: Detect payment required via HTTP 402 status code
ai.summary: Payment-required detection now checks for HTTP 402 status codes in addition to custom error types. `isPaymentRequiredError` uses duck typing to identify AI SDK `APICallError` instances with `statusCode === 402`. `loopAgentSteps` re-throws errors matching this status, bypassing the previous `PaymentRequiredError` name check. Updates affect `cli/src/utils/error-handling.ts`, `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`, and `sdk/src/errors.ts`.

eli5.text: When you hit a billing wall, the assistant now catches it through a standard "payment required" response code from the server, alongside the older name-based check. Previously, some providers sent back that code but used a different error signature, so the assistant could blow past the stop sign and keep going until it threw a confusing error. Now, the same out-of-credits detection applies to both error styles, so the behavior is consistent regardless of how the backend labels the failure. This is live today for anyone running into that wall.
